description: §14.8.9 raw-egress fail-closed — a protected row reaching a LEVEL-1 `_={ … }=` inline foreign block (the §23.2.4a canonical form) fires E-PROTECT-004. Pins the fix for a second measured fail-open: the source-text detector this replaced tested `/(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_$])_\{/`, which matches only the LEVEL-0 `_{` opener, while the opener grammar is `_` + N `=` + `{`. So the very form SPEC §23.2.4a's own worked example uses walked past the gate at exit 0. Detection is now by NODE KIND (`kind === "foreign"`), which answers identically at every opener level.
rationale: §14.8.9 closed-world precondition (SPEC.md:8519-8525) names 'a `_{}` foreign-code block (§23)' as an egress the compiler cannot analyze; the interior is opaque BY CONSTRUCTION, which is precisely why the SHALL is unconditional. The leak here is concrete: the emitted slice runs `JSON.stringify(u)` on the tagged row, yielding a plain STRING of independent identity, and `_scrml_protect_redact` returns a non-object unchanged — so the protected column crosses the wire fully intact. provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S352 (dpa-029 Q1).
